question: arXiv:2209.00006v2 compares the best-fit spectra of its Galactic Center excess candidates when each is fitted together with ring-based templates. Which candidate gives the faintest excess, and how good is its fit? What does the paper say about the spectra of the candidates that include the boxy bulge? And how does the dark matter spectrum obtained with the ring-based templates compare with those spectra and with the dark matter result obtained with the astrophysics-based templates of Cholis et al.?

arguments.answer:
The faintest excess with the ring-based templates is the X-shaped bulge. It also gives the worst fit. In Tab. 1 its −2ΔlnL is +30, so it is worse than no excess at all, and its ΔlnB is −190.

The candidates that include the boxy bulge have very similar spectra. These are the boxy bulge alone, boxy bulge "plus" (with the nuclear stellar components), and boxy plus X-shaped bulge. The paper describes them as relatively soft, "compatible with having absorbed unmodeled diffuse flux".

The DM spectrum with ring-based templates is harder on average than those bulge-type spectra. It is similar in spectrum to the DM result with the astrophysics-based templates of Cholis et al., but lower in flux. It also shows "wiggles" between energy bins that neither DM annihilation nor millisecond pulsars predict.
